workflow_runs.display_title: docs: clarify that maxParamLength does not prevent ReDoS (#7140)

head_commit.message:
docs: clarify that maxParamLength does not prevent ReDoS (#7140)

Fixes #7082

The `maxParamLength` docs claimed the option protects regex routes
against ReDoS. It does not: in find-my-way 9.10.0,
`currentNode.regex.exec(param)` runs on the whole path segment
(everything up to the next `/`), and only the captured values are
compared against `maxParamLength` afterwards. With `maxParamLength: 10`
and `allowUnsafeRegex: true` on `/u/:id(^(a+)+$)`, an 11-char segment
takes about 10 ms, 27 chars about 357 ms and 29 chars about 1282 ms, all
ending in a 404. The actual ReDoS guard is the `safe-regex2` check
find-my-way runs at route registration, which is skipped only when
`allowUnsafeRegex` is `true`.

#### Changes

- The `maxParamLength` docs no longer claim ReDoS protection, explain
that the limit is checked against the captured values after the regex
has run on the full segment, and link to `allowUnsafeRegex`.

The code is unchanged: checking the length before `exec` would reject
segments that hold several regex params (e.g. `/:a(^\d+)-:b(^\d+)`)
whose combined length exceeds the limit while each captured value is
within it, so changing that is a find-my-way decision.

#### Checklist

- [x] documentation updated
- [x] run `npm run lint:markdown` on the changed file
- [x] commit message and code follow the [Developer's Certification of
Origin](https://developercertificate.org/) and the [Code of
conduct](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

workflow_runs.display_title: feat!: fail closed when a response content type is not declared in th…

head_commit.message:
feat!: fail closed when a response content type is not declared in the content map

When a route declares a per-media-type (`content`) response schema but the
response `Content-Type` is neither a declared key nor `*/*`, the payload was
previously serialized with a raw `JSON.stringify`. That fallback bypassed the
response schema and could expose fields the schema was meant to strip.

The route response path now fails closed. If the response content type is not
declared and no `*/*` catch-all matches, `getSchemaSerializer` throws
`FST_ERR_MISSING_CONTENTTYPE_SERIALIZATION_FN` and the reply is a `500`,
surfacing the misconfiguration instead of silently returning unsanitized data.

The error handler call path is unchanged: it still resolves the default error
serializer (requesting `failClosed: false`), so error responses are unaffected.

head_commit.message:
[Backport 5.x] feat: add routerOptions.compile to use find-my-way compiler mode (#7116)

Proposal:

Manual backport of #7096 to `5.x`: the automated backport failed with
conflicts, see
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/7096#issuecomment-6155131364.

Cherry-pick of fcba984c0a41d7cfacff5234e0594d3b561cb804 with these
conflict resolutions:

- `build/build-validation.js` / `lib/config-validator.js`: `main` moved
`allowUnsafeRegex`, `caseSensitive` and `constraints` into
`routerOptions`, which is not the case on 5.x. Only `compile: false` is
added, then the validator was regenerated with `npm run
build:validation`.
- `fastify.d.ts`: only `compile?: boolean` is added to
`FastifyRouterOptions`, without the `constraints` rework from v6.
- `fastify.js`: kept `VERSION = '5.12.7'`.
- `test/internals/initial-config.test.js`: kept the 5.x snapshot (no
`routerOptions` in the defaults).
- `lib/route.js`: added the `defaultInitOptions` import from
`./initial-config-validation.js`, which `main` already had and the new
`routerOptions.compile ??=` line needs.
- `test/router-compile.test.js`: on 5.x `initialConfig.routerOptions` is
only exposed when the user passes it, so the "defaults to false" test
asserts `undefined` instead of `.compile === false`. Everything else is
unchanged.

Note:

`.npmrc` also carries over the `min-release-age-exclude[]=find-my-way`
entry, needed until `find-my-way@9.10.0` is older than 7 days
(2026-10-17).

---------

Signed-off-by: Tony133 <a.tripodi133@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Matteo Collina <hello@matteocollina.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: add routerOptions.compile to use find-my-way compiler mode

Bump find-my-way to ^9.10.0 and add a `routerOptions.compile` option
(default `false`). When enabled, the router trees are compiled into
generated JavaScript on preReady, once all the routes are registered,
which makes route lookups 1.3x to 2x faster.

The routing function no longer binds `router.lookup` eagerly, because
`router.compile()` replaces it on the instance.

head_commit.message:
perf!: don't capture stack traces for invalid request errors

Errors that Fastify creates when it rejects an invalid request, such as a
failed schema validation, an invalid JSON body or an unsupported media type,
only had stack traces pointing at Fastify internals. Capturing them cost more
than the rest of the error response.

The default schemaErrorFormatter now creates FST_ERR_VALIDATION instead of
a plain Error.

workflow_runs.display_title: perf!: don't capture stack traces for invalid request errors

head_commit.message:
perf!: don't capture stack traces for invalid request errors

Errors that Fastify creates when it rejects an invalid request, such as a
failed schema validation, an invalid JSON body or an unsupported media type,
only had stack traces pointing at Fastify internals. Capturing them cost more
than the rest of the error response.

The default schemaErrorFormatter now creates FST_ERR_VALIDATION instead of
a plain Error.

Signed-off-by: Gürgün Dayıoğlu <hey@gurgun.day>

workflow_runs.display_title: docs: clarify headers validation is additive, not a sanitized view

head_commit.message:
docs: clarify headers validation is additive, not a sanitized view

The synchronous custom-validator success value for the headers part is
applied through the additive request.headers setter, which adds or
overrides on top of the raw request headers rather than replacing them.
Document that request.headers is the incoming request's headers (plus any
additive values) and not a sanitized or authoritative view, and that a
header validator cannot remove a header by omitting it from the value.
Applications needing an allow-listed header subset should build and consume
it explicitly from the validated data or request.raw.headers.

head_commit.message:
fix(validation): normalize header names in every schema subschema

Normalize header-schema property names to lowercase across every schema
position - properties, required, dependencies, dependentRequired,
dependentSchemas, and nested subschemas - so case-sensitive assertions match
Node's lowercased request headers. Header schemas referenced through an
external shared $ref are not reached by this normalization and now emit a
warning.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: canonicalize per-content-type schema keys at route registration

head_commit.message:
fix: canonicalize per-content-type schema keys at route registration

Normalize schema.body.content and response content keys to their
lowercase essence media type when compiling validators and serializers,
so a mixed-case key such as Application/JSON is matched consistently at
request/reply time against the normalized request.mediaType lookup.

Reject case-equivalent duplicate keys (application/json vs
Application/JSON) and non media-type keys at startup with clear errors
instead of silently overwriting or silently skipping validation.

workflow_runs.display_title: refactor(types)!: remove deprecated FastifyPlugin type (#6897)

head_commit.message:
refactor(types)!: remove deprecated FastifyPlugin type (#6897)

* fix(types): allow explicit http2: false in server options (#6888)

* docs: clarify what attachValidation exposes on request.validationError (#6891)

* docs: clarify what attachValidation exposes on request.validationError

The docs described `request.validationError` as carrying "the raw
validation result", and the inline example pointed only at
`.validation`. That wording implied the descriptive message had to be
rebuilt by hand, which is what prompted #5235.

`wrapValidationError()` in lib/validation.js runs `schemaErrorFormatter`
and `validationCompleted()` in lib/handle-request.js assigns that same
error to `request.validationError`. There is no raw-only path, so
`.message` is identical to the message sent when `attachValidation` is
unset.

List the properties actually available (`message`, `validation`,
`validationContext`, `code`, `statusCode`) and add a test pinning the
equivalence between the attached and the default message.

* test: improve validation error message assertions in attached validation test

* refactor(types): remove deprecated FastifyPlugin type

Removed the deprecated FastifyPlugin type export and its corresponding test definitions. Users should use FastifyPluginAsync or FastifyPluginCallback instead.

* fix: update url

---------

Co-authored-by: Tiziano Basile <tiz.basile@gmail.com>
